notes.title: What’s Next for Spellcraft
notes.content:
[b]tl;dr:[/b] Thank you for playing in Preseason 1! We’re aiming to bring you Preseason 2 of Spellcraft in late June during Steam Next Fest (June 19th - 26th) with a team-based game mode that builds on our core gameplay while letting you squad up with friends.

To the Spellcraft community:

THANK YOU for joining us for our first ever public alpha – Preseason 1. The One More Game team has been poring over data from all of Spellcraft matches you played, re-watching VODs from Twitch streams, and reading all of the thoughtful feedback you shared over the 10 days of the test.

During Preseason 1, we released balance and bugfix patches almost every day. We knew the moment we put Spellcraft in front of thousands of players, we’d be almost immediately surprised about which Heroes, Spells and strats became dominant — and we believed it was important to act early and often to steer the game towards a relatively balanced state. We also released new content in the form of two new Heroes! You might not know, but everyone’s favorite eight-legged boy, Squiddleston, only made it into the alpha a day or two before we went live. And then we decided to drop #1 Interdimensional Nacho Fan Worldwide, Tony, into the game midway through the test, because we heard players asking for another tank.

In addition to two new Heroes and daily balance patches, the countless matches you played pushed us to replace the ‘Bleed’ mechanic with ‘Poison’. After a number of adjustments during the test, it became clear that the downward pressure afforded by spreading Bleed – coupled with the nature of the Team Wipe & Overtime win conditions – meant that we needed to remove the mechanic. Removing a mechanic that has been present in Spellcraft for the last two years, and doing so on a public stage should have been harrowing for the development team, but our tools and your feedback gave us the confidence we needed.

That mode of game development — listening to what players are telling us and acting fast — is how we will continue to operate. On that note, we wanted to share what we’re working on next, and what you can expect from Spellcraft moving forward:

[h2]1. Build On What We’ve Got[/h2]

First and foremost, a lot of you told us you like the video game we made. Hooray! No one’s made a “real-time battler” before, and we couldn’t be sure it was something players would love until we put it in your hands.

Internally we use scaling a mountain as an analogy for finding fun. You go up the mountain, check out the view, and decide if the route you took brought you to the highest peak with the best view. After earlier playtests, we’ve made the difficult choice to “go down, find another route, and go back up the mountain”. This amounts to making significant, fundamental changes to Spellcraft’s gameplay. Past versions of Spellcraft, while retaining similar vibes, have played quite differently. This time, we believe the core gameplay — controlling a team of heroes who bring powerful spells to the fight, and making upgrade choices between rounds to progress your agenda or counter your opponent’s strategy — resonates with enough players that we’re going to continue to build on this foundation.

Future versions of Spellcraft should continue to feel like the Spellcraft you just played…only MORE™. More Heroes, more Items, more improvements to game systems, UI, matchmaking — oh, and different ways to play with your friends and maybe make some new ones…

[h2]2. It’s Time to Team Up[/h2]

One of the most common questions we heard during Preseason 1 was: “how can I play with my friends?” It’s a question we’ve asked ourselves about Spellcraft since the earliest days of development, and just as common in previous closed alpha tests.

We’ve never intended Spellcraft to be limited to a pure 1v1 competitive game. We’ve been building it as such for a lot of reasons, like the fact that player population requirements are less of a challenge for a 1v1 game, and iterating on the 1v1 experience allowed us to focus on developing a novel core interaction model.

The next time we put Spellcraft in front of a lot of players, it’ll be with a team game mode at its center. You’ll be able to squad up with friends and play together in a shared match, with opportunities to collaborate on strategy and change things up against your opponents throughout. The exact shape of this game mode is in the works, and we’ll have more to share about what we’re building soon.

What we can share are the feelings we’d like to capture that 1v1 Spellcraft was lacking, which are unique to a co-operative multiplayer game:

[list]
[*] Moments of Collaboration – For a meaningful co-operative experience, players need to be able to influence each other’s choices, provide help when another player is in need, and to pool their power for a big push.
[*] Moments of Heroism – A skilled player needs to be able to put the entire team on their back and carry them. To steal a moment from Counter-Strike, a player needs to be able to single handedly Ace Clutch the enemy team and diffuse the bomb.
[*] Moments of Mentorship – Learning to play a game with a high skill ceiling can be lonely, but it’s much more fun, easier, and quicker to get up to speed when you’re paired up with a knowledgeable friend.
[/list]

Plus, hanging out and playing together with friends is just a lot more fun. By introducing a cooperative team element to Spellcraft, we hope players will recruit their friends to play, show them the ropes, and get good together.

We’re not sure what the future is for 1v1 Spellcraft because the co-operative mode hasn’t fully taken shape. We’d like to keep 1v1 Spellcraft available in the form of Duels (see you outside of Orgrimmar, scrub), but as with everything – we’ll be listening to your feedback and will have another roadmap update for you after Preseason 2.

[h2]3. When Can We Play???[/h2]

The second most common question we’ve heard after Preseason 1 was “when can I play again?” As devs, that’s a [i]great [/i]question to hear!

Right now, our intent is to launch Spellcraft’s Preseason 2 as part of Steam’s Next Fest that’s planned to run from June 19th through the 26th. That’s a pretty aggressive timeline to achieve what we’re hoping to build — but we’re gonna give it a shot. There’s a chance our timeline might slip, and we’ll let you know if it does.

Besides that next [i]big [/i]test, we’re also going to be thinking about the right ways to bring smaller groups of players back between now and then as part of our GameLab program (our community of playtesters who’ve been giving us feedback on Spellcraft regularly since late 2020).

We’ll be reaching out to Crafters who played a lot during Preseason 1 about opportunities to test what we’re working on soon!

[b]Thank You![/b]

Thank you again for joining us for this crucial moment in Spellcraft’s history. Your feedback and gameplay gives us fuel, and we’re so excited to show you what’s next. Make sure to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1806210/Spellcraft/#game_area_purchase]wishlist Spellcraft on Steam[/url], join us on [url=https://discord.gg/spellcraft]Discord[/url], and follow us on [url=https://linktr.ee/playspellcraft]social media[/url]. We’ll be sharing a lot more now that we’ve finally revealed Spellcraft’s gameplay, and we hope you’ll join us on the journey.

notes.title: Patch Notes - April 14th, 2023
notes.content:
[h2][b]Developer Notes[/b][/h2]

Hey Crafters! 

Small balance patch today with some minor bug fixes. Just over two more days until the Public Alpha ends and the servers go down. Make sure that you’ve finished your placement matches to secure your special Preseason One emblem.

[h2][b]Patch Notes[/b][/h2]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where stunning a unit would remove FBSS's attack speed stacks even if the unit did not switch targets. Thanks for the report @LastKardax

[*] Fixed a bug where pre-casting a basic spell on cooldown would not allow you to switch to casting an available respawn spell. Thanks for the report @TheRang

[*] Fixed some attack hit VFX being oriented incorrectly
[/list]

[u][b]Gameplay[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Solna: Reduced the duration of Block from 0.75s to 0.5s

[*] Solna: Holy Light recharge rate reduced 12s -> 13s

[*] Aster: Ensnare no longer deals damage, it is purely a utility stun. Reduced energy requirement 1500 -> 1250

[*] Ulla: Adding a small delay to Frost Shock to allow for counter-play opportunities and improved VFX so that players know who she is targeting
[/list]

[u][b]Art[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Tony got a new base, so he’s chilling on his bean bag, watching his favorite show. Unfortunately, Tony has eaten all of his Nachos, but we’re cooking up a fresh batch and will serve them up over the weekend!
[/list]

[u][b]UI/UX[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] When respawning unit’s, their respawn location and initial attack target are now previewed
[/list]

Please let us know what you think of the changes in the [url=https://discord.com/channels/760169602905800727/1087616177079058472]game-feedback forum[/url].

notes.content:
[h2]Developer Notes[/h2]
Hey @Crafters! 

Hope you are all enjoying Tony being thrown into the mix. Now that we’ve got some initial data on how our favorite stone boy is doing we are tweaking some of his spells.

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]

notes.title: Hotfix - April 12, 2023
notes.content:
[h2]Developer Notes[/h2]
Hey Crafters! 

We just couldn’t wait for tomorrow’s balance update to deliver some fixes. It seems adding a third tank helped some players discover that the 'increased damage taken' debuff was no longer being applied after a prolonged duration of Overtime. Thank you Ayden Pride and Tasty for your late night discovery!

[h2]Hotfix Notes[/h2]

[u][b]Gameplay[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] The ‘Shootout’ debuff will be applied to each Hero during Overtime once 60 seconds have elapsed. ‘Shootout’ increases damage taken by all Heroes by 10%, stacks indefinitely, and cannot be dispelled. If a Hero respawns while ‘Shootout’ is being applied, it will spawn with the same number of stacks as all other Heroes on the board.
[/list]

Please let us know what you think of the changes in the [url=https://discord.gg/spellcraft]game-feedback forum on Discord[/url].

notes.title: Patch Notes - April 12, 2023 - New Hero: Tony!
notes.content:
[h2]Developer Notes[/h2]
Hey Crafters! 

We’re over the moon by the response to the Spellcraft Public Alpha. Thank you so much for playing, streaming, and sharing feedback. We’ve been dropping a balance patch almost every day for the duration of the test, looking at data about how various strategies, Heroes and spells are performing across the MMR spectrum, and reading all of your feedback about how the game’s feeling. We’re back with another patch – this time with a big surprise.

One common request we’ve read was that it’d be nice to have another tank to choose from in the lineup, and so we decided to drop one. Here’s what Tony’s all about:

Tony is a disruptive tank who is not very fond of spell damage so when he drops below a certain health threshold he will gain massive spell resistance to shut down the haters.

Both of his basic spells will interrupt/stun enemies: one version hits all enemies in a line, while the other makes him fly across the map to interrupt one enemy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42381254/14ab2cc2baed61bf5f3b0ecc1502a1713d78ed85.jpg[/img]

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] All MMR adjustments that were lost during our service outage have been restored, showing that Eurantien, not Arroz_con_Mango, was the first player to achieve Sovereign! Congrats Eurantien!
[*] The Sovereign ranked emblem should now properly display for players on the leaderboard.
[*] Fixed some text expanding outside a background on match summary
[*] “Hover Links” for upgrade descriptions will auto expand in the team builder, previously only links for the non upgraded spell were displayed.
[/list]

[u][b]Gameplay[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Added a new Tank Hero to the game – Tony, the Royal Guard.
[*] Xaev and Aster respawn abilities will always attempt to target the hovered row as long as there is an empty space for the hero to spawn
[*] Zap magic damage amp 30% → 40%
[*] Zap upgrade magic damage amp 50% → 60%
[*] Rocket Jump now restores 100 barrier on use
[/list]

[u][b]UI/UX[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Added a Patch Notes button to the home screen
[*] When hovering gems on the match summary screen, the stats for that round is displayed. Clicking will lock to displaying that round as it previously did.
[*] The item selection UI has widened a bit because it’s been sneakily eating candy bars out in the garage
[/list]

Please let us know what you think of the changes in the [url=https://discord.gg/spellcraft]game-feedback forum on Discord[/url].

notes.title: Patch Notes - April 11, 2023
notes.content:
[h2][b]Developer Notes[/b][/h2]

Hey @Crafters! Welcome to buff day! We took a pass at spells that were underperforming and put some more oomph behind them. Also, we are experimenting with showing one additional item during the item phase. This means you will now always see one item per category. Finally, we’ve rebalanced the MMR brackets to better represent the current volume of players. We will adjust this again in future tests as the community grows.

Please keep telling us what you think in the [url=https://discord.com/channels/760169602905800727/1087616177079058472]game-feedback forum[/url]!

[h2][b]Patch Notes[/b][/h2]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Updated Vampirism Spell Vamp % to match the actual value 30% -> 40%

[*] Fixed a bug where Thorns would trigger on damage dealt effects. This only affected Reset’s attack speed passive but we avoid future bugs (phew)

[*] You can now bind right mouse button as a hotkey

[*] Fixed a bug where Shadow Dance could be continuously used FOREVER. FOR-E-VERR…
[/list]

[u][b]Competitive[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Ranked tiers have been rebalanced! Players should be able to rank up in ~2-3 games won against equally ranked players. 

[*] Players should see a substantial change in their current ranks. Players previously in Gold should see themselves in Platinum or even Diamond.
[/list]

[u][b]Gameplay[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Players will now be shown 4 items instead of 3 at the item phase. This means you will now always see one item per category.

[*] Rocket Jump cooldown reduced 6s -> 5s

[*] Rocket Jump Upgrade cooldown reduced 3s -> 1s

[*] Rocket Jump + Magnetic Pull/Push should now feel more responsive to use

[*] Ignite now scales off of Spell Power (50% SP base)

[*] Upgraded: 100% SP 

[*] Ignite Upgrade now spreads burning to ALL enemies on the board

[*] Combust on Burning targets now deals TRIPLE damage.

[*] Ice Lance cooldown reduced 7s -> 5s

[*] Frost Shock base now fully recharges when hitting an enemy with 5 stacks of frostbite

[*] Zap now scales with Spell Power instead of Attack Damage

[*] Zap spell power scaling increased 100% -> 200%

[*] Upgraded: 200% -> 400%

[*] Zap magic damage amp increased from 25% -> 30% and duration increased from 2s -> 5s

[*] Open Wounds starting charge count 0 -> 1

[*] Open Wounds cooldown reduced 7s -> 6s

[*] Open Wounds AD scaling increased 50% -> 100%

[*] Upgraded: 150% -> 200%

[*] Needle cooldown reduced 5s -> 4s

[*] Shadow Dance damage increased 50 (+50% AD) -> 100 (+100% AD)

[*] Upgraded: 100 (+100% AD) -> 200 (+200% AD)

[*] Tweaked description of Shadow Dance to make sure players learn they must RECAST this spell manually.

[*] We were seeing many players using this ability once during the activation period

[*] Cursed Circlet now triggers on any damage dealt, not just auto attacks. (Thank you Strohm!)
[/list]

[u][b]UI/UX[/b][/u]

[list]
[*] The in-world scoreboard is now visible post combat

[*] Player nameplates are now visual post combat
[/list]

Please let us know what you think of the changes in the [url=https://discord.com/channels/760169602905800727/1087616177079058472]game-feedback forum[/url]! forum.

notes.title: Patch Notes - April 7, 2023
notes.content:
[h2][b]Developer Notes[/b][/h2]

Hello Crafters!

We’ve been listening to all of your thoughtful feedback, tuning into your live streams, and crunching the numbers, and we’re about to push out a balance and bugfix patch.

During these tests the development team is greeted every morning with the play metrics from the previous day. Tests like this are how we figure out what is broken, what is fun, and what could be fun (or more fun) if we made some tweaks.

Big changes this patch include a Europa tweak that should rein her in early in the match, while still letting her scale into a menace as Spell Power items come online. We’ve also poked and pulled at Bleed strats that were becoming a bit too dominant. And while we know Cage is counterable – especially at higher ranks – his Slam Dunk was a little overtuned.

Those balance changes and more, plus bug fixes, art and UX improvements, all going live right now. The game client will prompt you to restart and patch before your next match.

We'll continue to listen to feedback and look at data throughout the entire test to maximize learnings and ensure the game continues to be fun and doesn’t get stale. Thank you for playing so many games! Let us know what you think in the #game-feedback forum. We’ll see you in ranked queue!

[h2][b]Patch Notes[/b][/h2]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]

● “Invite to Game” on the main menu will now work after playing a Custom game.

● Fixed a bug where Giant Slice was dealing 250 less damage than expected to center space

[u][b]Known Issues[/b][/u]

● Sometimes Spell Scrolls aren’t visible in your Spellbar but are still castable with hotkeys.

[u][b]Gameplay[/b][/u]

● If your “Swab the deck” target tile is occupied, it will now prefer falling back to farther unoccupied spaces instead of closer.

● Bleed replaced with Poison. Poison increases physical damage and healing received by 5% per stack

--● Needle starting charge count 3 -] 1. Damage increased 1 -] 50. Upgraded damage 50 -] 100

--● Razertips Volley renamed to Corrosive Volley

--● Eviscerate damage decreased 200 (+200% AD) -] 150 (+150% AD) to compensate for how much harder this will now hit with Poison stacks.

● Our goals with Europa tweaks is to reduce her early damage a bit while still letting her scale into a menace as Spell Power items come online

--● Missile damage decreased 700 (+300% SP) -] 400 (+350% SP)

--● Missile Upgrade base damage decreased 1500 -] 1200

--● Grenade damage decreased 400 → 300

--● Grenade Upgrade damage decreased 600 → 450

--● Orbital Strike tweaks

----● Center damage decreased 1500 -] 1200

----● Upgraded damage decreased 2000 -] 1750

----● Orbital Strike ring damage decreased 750 (+100% SP) -] 600 + (150% SP)

----● Upgraded ring base damage decreased 1000 -] 875

● Ion Strike damage decreased 1500 -] 750

● Slam Dunk KO thresholds decreased 30/50% -] 25/35% respectively

● Restricted Zone AOE damage amp decreased 30% -] 20%. Fixed wording to ensure clarity that this is a global buff

● Shatter damage increased 500 -] 1000

● Frost Blink can be used to cancel out of Blizzard

[u][b]Art[/b][/u]

● Warding Dome visuals have been updated

● Improving readability of Meteor and Meteor Trail telegraph VFX

[u][b]Audio[/b][/u]

● Updated “Choose an item” voice line

● Fixed some 3d positional audio issues

[u][b]UX & UI[/b][/u]

● Ranked banner added to scoreboard

● The board will no longer be colored red when immediately trying to cast a spell that has just been cast

Please let us know what you think of the changes!

notes.title: Patch Notes - April 6, 2023
notes.content:
[h2]Developer Notes[/h2]
Hello Crafters!

What an awesome first day of public alpha! Hope you’re all enjoying the game and climbing the ladder. We’re dropping a quick patch to address a couple of bugs and balance concerns we’re seeing.

Our goal is to ensure strategies are generally balanced, and that no one team is uncontestable. Bleed comps were feeling a little too spicy, so we’re tuning a few things based on the early data and feedback we’re reading.

Additionally, we’re squashing a whole buncha bugs. Thank you so much for your feedback, bug reports, and just for playing Spellcraft!

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]
Spellcraft v1.20545

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where Open Wounds Upgrade said Ines leaped to target when this isn’t the case
[*] Fixed a bug where Warding Dome wouldn’t immediately removes Spell Ward effect from allies when KO'd
[*] Fixed a bug where using Overpower on enemies only applied Burning for 5s instead of 10s
[*] Fixed a bug where Rocket Jump Upgrade wasn't actually recharging faster
[*] Fixed a bug where Squiddleston’s basic spells were not able to interrupt his Ultimate or Respawn spell
[*] Fixed issue with backing out of team select right as you were connecting to a match
[*] Fixed “new team” naming prompt not showing all team members
[*] Fixed some instances of units “warping” to their target tile instead of animating
[*] Fixed “auto respawn” not toggling during a match
[*] Fixed “ability” UI text string reference, and changed it to “spell”
[*] Fixed “relic” UI text string reference, and changed it to “item”
[*] Fixed “Overtime” Help and Tutorial strings for punctuation and description clarity
[/list]

[b]Known Issues[/b]
[list]
[*]Sometimes Spell Scrolls aren’t visible in your Spellbar but are still castable with hotkeys.[/list]

[b]Gameplay
[/b][list]
[*] Bleed damage decreased 20 → 8 per stack per second
[*] Bleed duration decreased 20s → 15s
[*] Open Wounds recharge decreased 8s -> 7s
[*] Solna's Block starting usage count 2 -> 1
[*] Razertips Volley base damage increased 100 -> 200
[*] Razertips Volley Upgrade base damage increased 200 -> 400
[*] Divine Intervention now instantly cleanses target ally
[/list]

notes.title: This Is Spellcraft!
notes.content:
Hello, gamers! We’re One More Game, and this is our first game: Spellcraft.

Spellcraft is a new type of strategy game: a [b]Real-Time Battler[/b] where you actively command an entire team of heroes and cast spells to outplay your opponents. Heck yeah! Blog post complete! Err...

We’d love to tell you a little bit about how we made this thing.

We chose our studio’s name as an aspiration: we want to make things that get players to say, “Alright, just one more game!” In other words, we want to make games players love.

Our team’s been lucky enough to work on a bunch of well-loved games over our collected careers. One of our founders, Pat, led development on some other games with “Craft” in the name, like, y’know, Warcraft and StarCraft (plus he cofounded ArenaNet for you enlightened Guild Wars heads). The team’s worked on a bunch of other games, too, like League of Legends, Magic: the Gathering, Pokémon, Diablo, et cetera.

We’re thrilled (and anxious!) to see how players react to Spellcraft. Here’s a little bit of background about how we came up with the game:

[h2]Genre Bending[/h2]

We knew that more than anything else, we wanted to build something new.

Not a “better version” of some established genre. Not yet another open-world action game with some big IP attached to it. We weren’t interested in chasing the latest trends, be they crypto, web3, the metaverse, or AI. We just* wanted to make a genuinely novel game that we hope players will want to play over and over again.

*lol

Early on, we thought about how our favorite online gaming experiences made us feel, and what would need to be true about our first game to capture some of that same energy.

We agreed on a few goals for our debut: it would be a multiplayer, competitive game. We wanted to balance an incredibly high skill ceiling with approachability for new players: as much love as we have for StarCraft, we wanted to make a game that doesn’t require superhuman APM to even compete.

We also decided we wanted to make a game that could theoretically be played – and played well! – on any gaming device*: PC, consoles, handhelds, (don’t you guys have) phones, VR/AR, Some Weird Device Elon Musk Wants to Implant in our Brains, etc.

*But we’re on PC only for now.

For a long time, when we talked about Spellcraft in private, we’d describe it half-jokingly as “real time, and strategic, but not real-time strategy.” Being in command of an entire army while a battle takes place in real-time is a unique sensation. But RTSes can be overwhelming and demand a lot of tedious micromanagement that many players don’t love.

We wanted to zoom in on the action while still making you feel like you were in control of a real-time battle. What if you were in command of an entire team in an MMO arena match – or a MOBA teamfight?

[h2]Alpha-Driven Development[/h2]

The hard thing about making something unprecedented and undefined is there’s no map or how-to guide. Finding the fun in a brand-new genre is one part modern art, one part mad science experiment. It requires both overwhelming hubris (“why yes, of course we can invent a new type of video game”) and selfless humility (“why yes, that brilliant design idea we were 110% confident in last week turned out to be a big ole stinker”).

[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/42381254/b3d4528bb54897989ae25160bab717d3b4d6e9c0.png[/img]

Our approach to navigating the part of the map that says “here be dragons” is something we call Alpha-Driven Development. Basically, that means we move fast, we involve external players early, and we focus on the core of what makes a game fun (over the polish and content).

We’ve been testing Spellcraft with external players almost every week since Halloween night in 2020. Having external players helps with the hubris and the humility: when real-live players tell us something we made is really fun, it confirms that we’re onto something – and it’s a morale-boosting shot of confidence for the team. On the flip side, external players have a perspective that’s free from the bias of, you know, being paid to work on a video game, and not infrequently players will tell us when something sucks for reasons that are hard to see when you’re close to it.

If you’re truly gamedev-pilled, and you want to read more, we’ve got a whole series of blog posts on our [url=https://www.onemoregame.com/blog]CORPORATE WEBSITE[/url] about how we think about makin' games.

[h2]Opening Up[/h2]

Until now, we’ve run two “larger” alpha tests with a few thousand players. Both alphas gave us confidence to believe we’re onto something with Spellcraft – and they also gave us plenty of feedback to ruminate as we steer the game towards something players might love.

Those alpha tests were confidential. We didn’t let anyone stream the game. We didn’t show any footage of the game in action. We didn’t even talk about what made Spellcraft’s gameplay unique. So while we learned a ton from those tests, we really don’t know how the game’s going to land with players once we really put it out there.

This alpha’s different. It’s a public playtest. Press one button on Steam and you’re in (unless we’re too popular for our own good)! We’re past being protective about what we’re making – it’s time to put it out there and see what the gaming public has to say. We’re working with content creators (BTW, if you make content, you should sign up for our creator program), and we’re putting Spellcraft in front of the media for the first time.

So, this is Spellcraft. It’s a real-time battler. Pick your heroes, place ‘em on the battlefield, and then you’re in charge. Nuke your opponent’s squishies, yeet your own dudes to safety, and devise your meta-crushing* strat to climb the alpha ranked ladder.

*Yeah, we’re pretty sure there will be an established meta by day 2 of the playtest – such is live game development. We’ll have some nerfs and buffs out soon to shake things up, don’t worry!

It’s an exciting moment for us. We hope you check out Spellcraft and agree that it’s something special. And we hope that you’ll tell us what you think, one way or the other.
